question.knowledge_point: Finding an Integral Representation For an Arc Length
question.problem: The length of the curve $y=x\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ on $[1,e]$ is given by
question.worked_solution:
The arc length of a curve $y=f(x)$ between $x=a$ and $x=b$ can be found using the formula

$$
L={\int }_{a}^{b}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=x\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ $a=1,$ and $b=e.$

First, we find the derivative of $f(x):$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x\cdot \frac{1}{x}=\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1
$$

Substituting ${f}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1$ into the arc length formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\sqrt{1+[{f}^{′}(x)]^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\sqrt{1+{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\sqrt{{ln}^{2}⁡x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
